flashcard_questions.q: Why are files compressed before being sent over a network?
flashcard_questions.a: They use less storage space and travel faster, using less bandwidth.

flashcard_questions.q: What does lossless compression do to a file?
flashcard_questions.a: It makes the file smaller without losing any information at all.

flashcard_questions.q: What can always be done with a losslessly compressed file?
flashcard_questions.a: The original can be rebuilt perfectly, bit for bit.

flashcard_questions.q: What is redundancy in a file?
flashcard_questions.a: Data that is repeated or predictable and can be stored more efficiently.

flashcard_questions.q: How does run-length encoding shrink a file?
flashcard_questions.a: It stores a repeated value once with a count of how many times it repeats.

flashcard_questions.q: How would run-length encoding record forty identical white pixels?
flashcard_questions.a: As 'white, 40' rather than writing the colour forty times.

flashcard_questions.q: What kind of image does run-length encoding work best on?
flashcard_questions.a: Images with large blocks of a single colour.

flashcard_questions.q: How does Huffman coding reduce the number of bits needed?
flashcard_questions.a: It gives the most common characters the shortest binary codes.

flashcard_questions.q: What does lossy compression permanently do to a file?
flashcard_questions.a: It removes some of the data for good, so the original cannot be recovered.

flashcard_questions.q: Which detail does lossy compression usually choose to discard?
flashcard_questions.a: Parts that humans are unlikely to notice.

Which sounds does an MP3 remove to shrink a song?
flashcard_questions.a: Sounds that are hard for the human ear to pick out.

flashcard_questions.q: Why does re-saving a lossy file repeatedly damage its quality?
flashcard_questions.a: The process is not reversible, so each save removes even more detail.
